output.question: What is Hims & Hers Health's short interest?
output.answer: The latest figure I found is for the October 30, 2026 settlement date. On that date 51,657,110 shares of Hims & Hers Health (NYSE: HIMS) were sold short, which is about 24.38% of its float of roughly 211.9 million shares, with 5.84 days to cover. That was down 1,815,985 shares (-3.40%) from October 15, 2026, when 53,473,095 shares were short (25.24% of float, 5.01 days to cover). Short interest has been falling since it peaked at about 41.25% of float on February 27, 2026. A Benzinga article that Webull shows as published about two days ago (early November 2026) gives a rounder 23% and calls HIMS one of the most shorted mid-cap stocks.

key_facts.fact: As of the Oct 30, 2026 settlement, HIMS had 51,657,110 shares short, or 24.38% of float (float of 211,881,389 shares), with 5.84 days to cover.
Short interest fell by 1,815,985 shares (-3.40%) from the prior settlement date.
As of the Oct 15, 2026 settlement: 53,473,095 shares short, 25.24% of float, 5.01 days to cover.
Short interest peaked at 41.25% of float on Feb 27, 2026 and has fallen since.
Benzinga (via Webull) reported short interest of 23% and called HIMS one of the most shorted mid-cap companies.

passages.quote: As of October 30, 2026, HIMS had 51,657,110 shares short, a 24.38% short interest based on float (211,881,389 shares). The position fell by 1,815,985 shares (-3.40%) from the prior settlement date. Days to cover was 5.84.
one of the most shorted mid-cap companies with a short interest of 23%

caveats: The ChartExchange text above is a summary returned by the page-fetch tool, not a verbatim quote from the page. The numbers come from exchange/FINRA short-interest reports filed twice a month, and newer data may come out soon.
Percentages depend on the denominator. ChartExchange uses float, so its figures differ from those based on shares outstanding, which is a likely reason other outlets report about 23%.
The Benzinga/Webull article gives no exact publication date (only '2d ago') and does not name the source of its 23% figure.
MarketBeat and Chartmill blocked access (HTTP 403), so I could not use them to cross-check.
